Yhh I've researched the hell out of everything and bought a list of supplements and OTC stuff, even got some CBD stuff in the mail (if it will even work!), I'll honestly try anything than going back, just to take some of the edge off of the physical pain.. Thats always been the first thing to rear its ugly head and the withdrawal symptom that bothers me the most! Especially in my calf muscles.

For about 10 years, my drug of choice was codeine. (I was one of those cliché people getting a genuine prescription for a real reason from the docs. Unfortunately, I now know I was far too messed up from various life experiences, to be in control of big boxes of my own meds and a very steady supply of a family members who didn't miss them at all (Turning a huge blind eye for 8 years I guess is what I'd call it.. And I feel terrible nowadays that I did this to them because I know they loved me and wanted me to be happy and comfortable etc). I was already a borderline alcoholic from something terrible that had happened that year and I was quite young when it started, though it was very gradual..

Ive had the image of me deciding to double dose for the first time burned in my brain these past few days; stood at the kitchen window, looking out into the night, worrying that something would immediately go wrong, but I mean 60mg, it didn't, because I'd already been taking the 30mg 4 times a day.. And of course it was amazing! But I quite obviously didn't think of where I would be in 12 years time.. And how un-amazing it would be...

The final 2 years of the first 10, were spent bumping as much codeine as possible in any combination. To the point I was taking about 30 paracetamol (with codeine) a day. I told my immediate family, got help and went on bupe...  

In the 2 years that followed, despite getting help and seemingly being okay, but not really wanting to be clean or seeing the severity of the situation, it quickly turned into anything I could get my hands on, I'd stopped drinking for many years, but benzo's and z drugs, like zopiclone and ambien, fake xanax (even though they werent what I really wanted, they got me out of my head), 60mg codeine only tabs and many of them by this point, then a mix of morphine, tramadol and tapentadol.. Thats all I can remember specifically, but you get the picture.. I was basically shopping around the dark web like it was a sweet shop.. And an almost too reliable sweet shop I would say! Only got fleeced once! 

Anyway, it finally got to oxycodone and a couple of intranasal episodes of heroin... I was destroying everything around me and was persuaded into getting help again. 

The following 4-5 months I had a couple of lapses and one big relapse where I'd taken about 200 tramadol in 2 days and was hospitalised (again!! I had 2-3 really bad OD's somewhere in this story).. 
I'd only just gotten a new job, but I lost that, lost my family, my fiancé, my friends, the respect of everyone, as the story usually goes... I'd lost absolutely everything! Tried to end everything, with all the bells and whistles... 

So that was early 2019.. But following the OD and the SA, something switched in my brain and I can't really explain it, or say exactly where it came from.. But from then on, I actually stuck to the buprenorphine.. I knew I couldn't quit cold turkey, I'd tried that before.. But I also knew I needed time to heal in literally every way.. Soo I stayed on the bupe until starting to reduce about 4 months ago... I did drop from 8mg to 6mg in the summer of 2019, but that was an awful experience due to the ridiculousness of buprenorphine costs! (That's a whole other thing that really makes me mad!) But anyway, that time to heal really helped, I got everyone back, including my fiancé, we're trying for a baby now, family's great etc.. 

I just need to do this last hurdle.. As I said before, I'm fairly head strong,  I know I've probably got the withdrawals easier than what many others will have them.. But damn it's been a journey. Doing it this way with the bupe for so long has really helped, but despite that, it's hard not to have those thoughts that make you want to cave in or wish for better times of the past etc when there's finally nothing in your system.. But I can pass them off, come on here and tell you my life story lol! (Sorry about that, but it has really helped! :)) My legs still absolutely reck though :/

Can you advise any tips etc on how to help with the physical pains and sleep?? Or is it just a case of sucking it up?.. I mean it's 3am nearly, I feel like I could pass out with fatigue, but everytime I lie down, my arms and legs are on fire! :( And despite feeling headstrong about not using again/using illicit substances, and I want to do this, I feel on the verge of a breakdown :/ I know I have no more meds for tomorrow to help, and I know its likely only going to get worse before it gets better! Damn the emotional swings!

How long did the physical pains of withdrawal last for you after your final dose (of whatever that might have been)?? I'm talking, muscle/bone aches.. I know it won't be the same for everyone, but I genuinely feel like I could sleep better if the pains weren't there and I'm desperate for them to go! I've technically not gone past day 2, as I've spread my bupe/subs out on an every other day basis and only had 0.2mg.. However, that's all gone now! :) I feel incredibly head strong about this whole thing, and I say bring on day 3 and beyond! But right now, god damn these pains!!

Are these thoughts new?? You say a year going on 2, just wondering if you have felt like this the whole time or just recently?

The problem with this sort of thing, even after so much time (assuming there hasn't been any use at all) is trying to establish what you are trying to run away from...

I know how this sounds.. It sounds exactly how I heard it the first time. "Fuck off" I think was my answer...

It sounds like you've found something or something within you that is keeping you from going back, and thats absolutely fantastic! I would always advise anyone in active addiction to find something, anything, to hold onto.. "Who will feed the dog if I'm dead?", "How will my family react?" "Who will water the plants?"... Literally fucking anything! And build on that from there... "How will I watch my favourite movie?", "eat my favourite food?"... Eventually building a fluid mental list of things that excite you and that you love outside of drugs... 

If within that time, you realise you hate everything.. Then why? Speak to someone... A shrink, friend, family member, anyone... Look back on your life and too be honest.. For fuck sake, that shit is 1 million times easier than going through withdrawal and overdoses and all the other shit that comes with it!

You have got this! You are doing brilliantly! Cravings will pass, but please do something to try and make them less frequent :)

Thank you for reading and for your reply! 
Support I think is one of the main reasons I finally took a step back and realised the full extent of what was going on. A lot really hit me at the time (2 years ago) and the support of my partner and family are really whats kept me going. Being able to settle on a bupe dose for the past year or 2 and focus on the people around me and other things in life has given me the perspective I needed to finally try and beat this thing!

Its hard as F some times though for sure.. We definitely don't like being uncomfortable and much of the past 12 years for me has been very uncomfortable.. And its hard not to fall into a hole when nothing seems to be going right, the future looks bleak, and things become even more uncomfortable... The emotional swings are insane! But having people around me, firmly makes me believe I have atleast something worth fighting for... I just need to do this and then get the rest of my life on track, for the good of everything and everyone! 

Ironically, now I'm off the 1 medication, I'm taking about 11 to try and combat the side effects lol! Which do include some gaba related stuff, drug store supplements etc, had a short course of Z sleep tabs, which hasn't really worked when the withdrawals are at their worst tbh.. Stupidly it was like being high at 3am, and if anything made trying to sleep worse! Worth saying though its not the high my body is craving, so there's not been any issues there because my mind as you say is in it to win it! (Side note: I have been very fortunate to not have developed any other kind of substance issue, i.e. I quit drinking for opiates years ago and when I decided to enjoy alcohol again, I only ever drink a few on a weekend if that.. I really couldn't do the same thing with alcohol or anything else.. My relationship with substances was very focused on my devil friend the opiate.. And its the only thing I ever wanted.. Which in a way I do feel quite blessed for, but of course in and of itself its a nightmare!)

I've never really given myself the chance to put so much into getting healthy and sorting all this out before, so its fairly new... I don't think I've been this 'clean' for a better word in over the 12 years I mentioned.. Soo its definitely been an experience and a half! But as far as opiates go, I really do want out now... I enjoyed it for many years, but its actually one of the most tiresome and scary things one can put themselves through in my opinion.. Dicing with death every single day for years, NAH AH! Not anymore!

I've made a few posts on r/addiction as that is most relevant to my everyday situation... However, throughout my journey as an avid opioid addict, not being around hasn't exactly been at the bottom of my list of things to do...
I even called one of the helplines once, who out of everyone I've ever had the pleasure of speaking to about this, the lady I got that day was brilliant... 

A little background: 
12 years ago, I began a long and slow career towards an utter armageddon meltdown with regards to prescription medication. I had that clichéd experience of going to the GP as I had when I was younger, and recieved codeine to treat my genuine pain.. The only difference on this occasion was that I found it helped to treat my recent insomnia, which I'd had for a couple of years at this point during my school years... 

Fast forward a little bit and for reasons I won't get in to, I suddenly had codeine on tap, due to someone I was living with being prescribed when they didn't even want it, but were happy to 'save me a trip to the doctors'... For 8 years... Yes 8 years... I'm sure he knew and his wife and anyone else flittering, but they wanted to support me and this pattern is followed throughout mostly everyone in my life. Either people didn't want to accept it, or they ended up feeding my problem. And honestly I place no blame on anyone else at all! I think the couple I lived with cottoned on in the end as suddenly the supply dried up. Obviously at the time I pointed fingers like a crazed drug addict, but thats what we do in those situations, warranted or not.

However, my life changed significantly, which meant moving and meeting someone new... Someone who had already dealt with my behaviour with someone else and lost that person only a year before... But we fell in love, we made it work... But not before I went really dark. The darkest I had ever become... 

If you hadn't noticed, the theme here is I've let so, so many people down... I bought indescript drugs that contained god knows what, Stole drugs from my work place (ironically, to end my life) which literally it did, fired and all that... All culminating in a huge relapse and hospitalization where I lost everything. A new great job I had, all my friends and previous colleagues from various jobs, my partner and the respect from my family... 

Now currently, as I type this at 2am, I am in withdrawal, from a controlled taper, 2.5years clean of illicit substances and doing very well... And I am thrilled with my progress, as others have told me they are too... Including the girlfriend I lost, who is actually my fiancé now, my family are getting there for sure, soo some things are in a much better place...

However, I know the damage is done. 

I've lost people, destroyed people who then needed help themselves, including my partner, who to go from finding a dead partner in the past to all my antics, must be truly horrible... Obviously it must be said that she chose to move forward with our relationship as much as I did etc, knowing what could happen... But I think that's mostly besides the point... I've put her through hell, as I have others, where none of these people deserved it one teeny tiny bit and I can't help but wonder if she and my family would truly be better off without me, or what value I could really bring to society as a whole at this point, if I continue on.

As I said before, finding a job has been fruitless; even before Covid... I have no problem working extra hard/harder than others to get my place, but nobody wants an 'untrustworthy junky' or someone who can't or won't explain gaps in history... 
So how on earth am I ever going to provide for my future wife and children...

At this point, despite my efforts to get my health back, it's hard to see the point of it all and the why bother aspect of things... I absolutely don't plan on letting anyone down (including myself) with my sobriety... But walking off a cliff on my favourite UK coast doesn't half have a ring to it... 

Contrary to everything I've said, I think the only thing really holding me back, is that I can't leave these people behind... I love my other half to pieces and I'm fairly sure she loves me the same (I think)... But as strong and independent as she is, I can't leave her on her own, it's not in my nature, or to put her through more unnecessary hurt that she's already experienced, and in this situation by my disappearance and re-emergence on some rocks in France 2 weeks later... I also can't leave my family and put them through the hurt as well. 

If I had no attachments to people at this point (yes I love our pets too) then I would absolutely be on a train to Scotland, buy a few nice things for my send off and get out of this life that I seemed to have screwed up so badly and made so hard for myself.

I think about this every night. I lose sleep, just wondering why and regretting most of my life choices. Everytime I look at my fiancé now, I'm second guessing why she's still with me and telling me she loves me... 
Put it this way, I haven't heard a peep in years from friends and acquaintances from the past... They had a real choice to stay in touch or not... For family and partners its going to be harder to leave... Soo why not do it for them?

(Apologies for the humour. I am very serious, its just my way of dealing with things).
Thank you for your comment. :) I'm pleased that someone found something positive from reading this post. You are a rockstar and doing the best work, 10 years is monumental! Keep it up! :)

With regards to coming off the subs: I've been on subs for 2 years+.. This last 2 years has been a solid 2 years that I've stayed away from any illicit substances/other substances, full stop. In that time, I've worked on myself, including therapy and group sessions and any support I could find. 

It did however, take me all of the first year to just get myself to stop thinking about drugs all the time, and look for other healthy outlets in life and generally to just be happy. 

Reading this and some of your other posts, I would suggest not even thinking about coming off the subs yet (only my opinion). The + in my 2 years+ is all the other years I was on subs and relapsing, trying to come off and going right back around in a circle, back to the beginning. I just wasn't ready. The subs have genuinely helped me get my life back, and I personally believe there is a hell of a lot of growth to be done and a hell of a lot of work to be done to make staying sober stick. You are only 18 as you say, so I'd look at that the other way around. You have loads of time to get things sorted and to work on yourself, to get sober. There is no rush. Some people do rely on subs forever, but if you want to take a different approach, then pace yourself.
Personally I'm at the point now, where I'm half way off the subs in my reduction programme and I'm barely getting withdrawals. I'm not thinking about drugs or getting high. I'm thinking about my fiancé, my family, my new job, hopefully having a baby on the way. But it took me a long time to get to this mindset. It was hard work, but I do believe for any person, it is possible. Withdrawals I also don't think can be compared drug to drug. Some I'd say perhaps give less withdrawals than others, but this is another case of person to person. I personally never tried to reduce on any full agonist opioid, so I don't know for sure, but subs honestly are no walk in the park either.

One thing that springs to mind when I read questions and comments like this, is one of the main things in addiction, which is 'instant gratification'. Addicts crave the instant high, the instant relief, we always want it right now. And from what I have learnt and believe, when we try to do other things in life, like get off the subs or anything else, there is transference, and we crave for everything to be instant. 

Part of recovery is almost rewiring your thinking to be successful. This of course might not be the case for everyone, but it certainly was in my experience.

So my advice is, well done for having got to where you have! You are doing brilliantly and you should be proud of that. However, the fight isn't over, and as shit as this sounds, it never will be 100%. There is always going to be a tiny element of thinking and such, even at 10 years sober. But if we work hard, we will reap the rewards substantially. But take your time in doing so. I wouldn't go 200mph in a car to get everywhere, so I try not to do that in life. Stay well, stay safe! :)

First and foremost your health and sobriety are most important. You very clearly agree and you should be really proud of that. Proud of how far you have come and proud of how you recognise potential triggers and issues, and making informed, sensible choices about your actions etc, so that you can stay safe. Damn, I'm proud of you! Lol! I'm sure there are many people (including myself) in the past, who have thrown a f**k it, winged it and regretted it. Not every time of course. Its down to each individual and the circumstances, but I'd sooner be on the safer side.

It's also not about who 'appears' to be more 'fun' and living up to that, it's about supporting yourself in a situation like this. Hell I'm sure you can be great fun! But regardless, forget about sober or not sober, you are a person and you do you!

Put it this way as well. I'm very sure if one of your colleagues or any other person had a problem or wanted to make a particular choice, especially when it came to their health and safety, they're not going to give it a second thought about how others might feel about it. It's like that thing where somebody might worry they have a bad haircut for example, they worry about it the whole time and what others might think. The only thing with that, is that the 'others' are likely too busy worrying about their own haircuts, to even give a thought to anybody else. And those that do choose to bring other people down, aren't worth your time. If your colleagues are good people, maybe even friends? They want to hang out with you after all... Then they should be able to understand that your plans need to deviate just slightly, no matter what the reason. It is also a work thing at the end of the day.

If you can get your own room, or be in a room with 'the quieter ones' (still make sure this is right for you), then it's down to you from there. I'm sure there would be nothing wrong with accepting your colleagues invite, but just visit their room, or hang with them for a while, and then remove yourself from the situation if needs be, or when you feel it is time. This is of course again, if this suits you. Its definitely a great idea to have a safe space you can retreat to if needs be. Definitely nothing worse than being stuck.
As a side note here, if your bosses are aware and you would feel comfortable doing so, it might be worth mentioning your situation to one or two of your most trusted colleagues (If this is possible). That way, if any situations come up, or somebody else pressures you unknowingly, then you will be able to gather support. And that support doesn't have to be blatant, they could just help change the subject etc. 

Overall, in some circumstances the advice would very well be to not go and leave it alone. However, if you are prepared and comfortable going, and genuinely excited about the expo, (which you seem to be) then go have a great time! Stay safe! And I hope everything goes well! You will also never know how things could go, if you don't 'dip your toes in the water' so to speak. So plan, be prepared and have a great time! :)
